faqs.q: The President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the elected members of:

faqs.q: The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of:

options.b: Only elected members of both Houses of Parliament
options.c: Elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament
options.d: Elected members of Parliament and state legislative assemblies

faqs.a: Elected and nominated members of both Houses of Parliament

faqs.q: Which of the following is a correct point of difference between the electoral college for the Vice-President's election and that for the President's election?

options.a: The President's electoral college includes nominated members, while the Vice-President's does not

options.c: The Vice-President's electoral college includes nominated members of Parliament, while the President's electoral college includes only elected members
options.d: The Vice-President's electoral college excludes Rajya Sabha members entirely

faqs.a: The Vice-President's electoral college includes nominated members of Parliament, while the President's electoral college includes only elected members

faqs.q: Why did Dr. B.R. Ambedkar justify excluding state legislative assembly members from the Vice-President's electoral college?

options.a: State legislatures lacked the administrative capacity
options.b: The Vice-President's normal function is to preside over the Council of States, and assuming presidential duties is rare and temporary
options.c: It would make elections too costly
options.d: The Constitution required uniformity in officer elections

faqs.a: The Vice-President's normal function is to preside over the Council of States, and assuming presidential duties is rare and temporary
